what_happened: In job bw7k (a code job), the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The request had three parts. Part (3) was a status report of median and slowest test-check durations. The reading split part of it off, or deferred it to a follow-up job. The user replaced it with a reading that does all three parts in this one job and splits no acceptance item into a follow-up.
cause: The reading stage does not compare its list of deliverables with the parts the request names, so nothing catches a part that goes missing. It also has no rule that a request's explicit parts are in scope for the job unless the user agrees to a split. The reading stage is trained to keep jobs small, because of the producer deadline and budget limits. The report part looks separable and cheap to defer, so the stage defers it. The reading is accepted without a check that every named part is a deliverable with a criterion. Only the user, who remembers what they asked for, notices. The existing class for reading too much (0952) is the reverse of this flaw.
prevention: Before a reading is accepted, run a check that extracts the numbered or lettered parts of the request, such as (1), (2) and (3). It requires each part to map to at least one deliverable and one acceptance criterion in the reading. It refuses any reading that moves a part to a follow-up, a later job or an "out of scope" note, unless the request itself says so. If the reading seems too big for one job, it should flag this to the user and not drop the part silently.
proposed_request: Make sure Athena's reading of a request covers every part the request names. Add a check, run before a reading is accepted, that finds the numbered or lettered parts of the request and confirms each one has a deliverable and an acceptance criterion in the reading. The check must refuse a reading that moves a named part to a follow-up job or marks it out of scope, unless the request itself asks for the split. The refusal message must name the missing part. Add tests with fixture requests: one with three parts and a reading that covers all three is accepted; one where the reading defers part (3) is refused and names part (3); one with no numbered parts is unaffected. Then replay the check over the last 50 real requests with accepted readings and report how many it would newly refuse.
